doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: Growing up on top 40 radio and The Police
summary: She describes pop music as her childhood drug, and how The Police's Synchronicity influenced her progressions.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I think what I’m after here is I have to admit I used to have an attitude about not just composers but pop musicians who didn’t have any theoretical background. And thankfully I got over it. Because I recognized that some of these musicians come up with things that I don’t think they would have done had they had a bunch of rules or ways to do things that they learned from somebody else. And so I’m just wondering if —

Definitely a more natural process of coming from a different place that is not chock full of harmony rules, but also more basic too because it’s not like they’re studying the classical art form of their instrument. That’s the best way I can put it. They’re just working on their sound and putting out. And to me that’s intriguing because I think it’s a place I go to. I was brought up on a lot of pop music. It was kind of my drug as a kid was to listen to top 40 radio and find things I liked. And I didn’t like everything. I really didn’t like everything but there was the odd thing I really liked.
